title: Data Operations Warrant Officer
raw_text:
8-255A. MOS 255A--Data Operations Warrant Officer
      a. Licensing/certification requirement. CompTIA Security+ CE or DOD 8570.01-M IAT Level II and
IAM Level I certifications.
      b. Prerequisites. DA PAM 611-21.
      c. MOS 255A. MOS 255A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is any MOS. All enlisted
MOS to include other military services who can substantiate their qualifications with performance
evaluations, awards, and certificates in information systems administration, mission command systems
administration, Local Area Network (LAN) administration, cybersecurity, or computer network defense as
assessed through the accession process meets current requirements.
      d. Associated SQIs.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
         (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
      e. Associated ASIs. Refer to table 6-5 for listing of universal ASI’s associated with all warrant officer
MOS. Q6--Protection Cell Operations (personnel only) (Effective 202410).
       f. Qualifications.
          (1) Physical Demands Category – Moderate (Gold).
          (2) WO1/CW2 must--
             (a) Be a U.S. citizen.
             (b) Must qualify for and maintain a Top Secret (TS) clearance with special compartmentalized
information (SCI) access. MOS 255A warrant officers will initiate procedures to obtain the proper level of
clearance immediately upon notification of the MOS 255A functional designation.
             (c) Meet vision and hearing standards of AR 40-501 for assignment of officers to Signal Corps,
normal color discrimination per AR 40-501, and have full use of both hands.
             (d) Successfully complete the MOS 255A Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC).
             (e) Minimum OPAT scores for physical demands category moderate (gold) are: Long Jump
(LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval
Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles.
             (f) DoD 8570.01-M IAM Level II and Information Technology certifications in the server,
application development, database, and cloud computing environments are desired.
         (3) CW3 must--
             (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f (1).
             (b) CW2s assigned to CW3 positions will be a graduate of MOS 255A Warrant Officer
Advance Course (WOAC) prior to assignment.
             (c) DoD 8570.01-M IAT Level III and Information Security certifications are desired.
        (4) CW4 must--
             (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f (2).
             (b) CW3s assigned to CW4 positions will be a graduate of WOILE prior to assignment.
             (c) DoD 8570.01-M CNDSP Infrastructure Support and IAM Level III certifications are desired.
        (5) CW5 must see MOS 255Z.
     g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2--
              (a) Designs, builds, configures, operates, maintains, and sustains information systems and
services within the Army’s portion of the cyberspace domain on the Department of Defense Information
Networks (DODIN).
              (b) Secures and protects data systems by maintaining a cybersecurity posture through the
implementation of cybersecurity policies and the use of electronic keys for information systems.
                 (c) Advises the commander or Signal operations officer on the management and operation
of Army information systems and services.
                (d) May serve as an Data Operations Warrant Officer in a Brigade Combat Team, Multi-
functional Brigade, Security Forces Assistance Brigade, or Expeditionary Signal Battalion Staff.
                (e) May serve as Data Operations Warrant Officer in a Functional Brigade or Ranger
Regiment Battalion Staff, Executive Communications Chief, or Sustainment Automation Support
Management Office (SASMO).
           (2) CW3--
               (a) Directs and performs duties described in paragraph g (1).
               (b) Trains and supervises cyberspace information technology personnel on the operation,
maintenance and sustainment of information systems and services enabling combat power projection for
mission command.
               (c) Focuses on data availability and content management by analyzing, collecting,
processing, storing, disseminating, and securing information on-demand to facilitate warfighting and non-
warfighting operations.
               (d) Advises senior staff members, decision, and policy makers on Army information systems
and services operations, training, policies, and procedures.
               (e) May serve as an Data Operations Warrant Officer of Functional Brigade, Division, ASCC,
or Joint staff.
               (f) May serve as an Data Operations Warrant Officer at Regional Cyber Center, National or
Joint Training Center, DISA, or WHCA.
               (g) May serve as an Instructor/Writer, Capabilities Developer, or Special Operations Forces.
               (h) May serve as the HRC SC Junior WO Assignments Manager or WOCC TAC Officer.
          (3) CW4--
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g (2).
               (b) Develops policy recommendations and provide technical guidance and advice to
Commanders and staffs on the management and operation of Army, Joint, intergovernmental,
interagency, and multinational information systems and services.
                (c) May serve as senior Data Operations Warrant Officer of Corps/ASCC/ACOM/Joint staff.
                (d) May serve as senior Data Operations Warrant Officer for Theater Signal CMD staff,
DISA, Regional Cyber Center, JITC, or WHCA.
                (e) May serve as senior Data Operations Warrant Officer as a Doctrine Writer or
Capabilities Developer.
                 (f) May serve as the HRC SC Senior WO Assignments Manager or in Nominative
Assignments.
       h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
           (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
           (2) Table 8-255A-1. Physical requirements.
           (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of three definable skill levels: W2
equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; and W4 equals CW4. The grades are listed in the following
standards of grade tables:
                  (a) Table 8-255A-1. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
                  (b) Table 8-255A-2. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
